Subject: EdgeWorks evaluation — proof-of-outcome checklist & MAP (draft)

Hi Julia / Alex —

Thanks for the conversation this morning. As promised, attached is a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short "proof-of-outcome" checklist we drafted to make the evaluation deterministic from a success / fail standpoint. High level:

- Goal: Validate a production-ready inferencing flow for EdgeWorks triage assistant with latency < 450ms median RPS on your sample traffic and token-level cost within the expected range.
- Acceptance tests (attached in acceptance_tests.md): functional smoke, concordance on a 500-prompt testset, latency distribution tests, and an incident/failover runbook check.
- Exit gates: (1) All critical smoke tests pass, (2) Concordance score >= 92% on labeled dataset, (3) No unplanned data egress during the pilot, (4) Procurement/contract terms signed or clear PO path.
- Owners: We propose Redwood owns runtime config & monitoring setup (Karthik, Marissa), EdgeWorks owns labeled evaluation set and procurement (Julia, Alex).
- Timeline proposal: 2-week pilot (week 1 ingest + baseline tests, week 2 tuned runs + final verification).

Please review the attached EW_MAP_v1.xlsx — the left column is the timeline and owners. If this matches your expectations I can update the SOW and route to procurement; if anything is missing, flag it.

Quick asks:
1) Confirm the labeled evaluation set can be shared to the secure S3 path by 09/10.
2) Confirm whether the data residency requirement is strictly "US-only" for the pilot or if regionally redundant staging is allowed.

I left a few optional acceptance checks as "stretch" targets (latency P95, long-form prompt concordance), we can shrink/expand based on what matters most to EdgeWorks.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0194

Subject: Re: EdgeWorks evaluation — proof-of-outcome checklist & MAP (draft)

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A few clarifying notes from EdgeWorks product + procurement perspective: 

- Labeled set: we can stage a de-identified 500-prompt set to a secured S3 bucket by COB 09/10. That works.
- Data residency: pilot needs to be US-only (for PHI-similarity constraints) unless we put a contractual exception in place — prefer to keep pilot in US for now.
- Acceptance tests: concordance >= 92% is acceptable but can we define the specific metric (exact match vs. semantic similarity)? For our internal scoring we'll use an F1-weighted semantic similarity with human adjudication on disagreements.
- Performance: can Redwood provide a short-run baseline report (simple RPS/latency profile) within 48 hours of ingest so we can see where tuning effort will fall?

Also cc'd our procurement alias (procurement@edgeworks.health) — they'll need the SOW and an initial PO template to expedite.

If we can get the map updated for US-only and we agree the confirmation checkpoints, we can kick off next Wednesday.

Cheers,
Julia Moreno
Head of Product | EdgeWorks Health

Julia / Alex —

Appreciate the quick feedback. Two small but important clarifications from Redwood ops side so the acceptance flow is unambiguous: 

1) Concordance metric: we'll add a dual-band check —
   - "Automated similarity" (embedding cosine + threshold tuned to your adjudicator) as the primary pass/fail gate, and
   - "Human adjudication" on the 50-sample disagreement set as the tie-breaker.

2) Performance baseline: we'll run an initial ingest + 1-hour steady-state at expected concurrency after you drop the dataset. Expect a short PDF report (RPS, median latency, P95, resource utilization) within 24 hours of the run if the data is available.

3) Failure/rollback gate: if any critical smoke test fails during the final verification (week 2), we automatically roll back to the canary config and open a joint incident review within 4 hours.

4) Evidence expectations for the acceptance bundle: logs (token-level cost breakdown), monitoring dashboard snapshot, and a short recording of the adjudication session (if any). We'll put a checklist in the MAP for each evidence artifact.

I've attached a redlined acceptance_tests.md and a draft SOW (SOW_Draft_v0.3.pdf) for procurement to review. If we get procurement contact + dataset by 09/10, the pilot schedule is feasible.

Proposed next steps (short):
- Karthik: update EW_MAP with US-only residency noted and the evidence checklist (today)
- Julia / Alex: confirm dataset drop + procurement contact (today)
- Marissa: prepare initial baseline runbook and monitoring template (tomorrow)
